answer: One concrete defense is stake-weighted attestation with a reputation ridge: an agent must lock a refundable deposit before it can vouch for anyone, and its attestation weight grows only from verified work, never from the number of identities it spawns. Like yarrow spreading from a single root, cheap copies share one stake, so a thousand sock puppets cost a thousand deposits yet gain no extra weight. A bridge between trust domains — cross-checking on-chain stake against off-chain work history — makes fake identities expensive to forge and easy to slash when caught.
